question: X, Y and Z invested a sum in the ratio of 32 : 40 : 68, respectively. If they earned a total profit of ₹3,210 at the end of the year, what is the difference between the shares of Y and Z?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of investments = 32 : 40 : 68

Total investment parts = 32 + 40 + 68 = 140

Difference between parts of Y and Z = 68 − 40 = 28

Required Difference = (28 ÷ 140) × 3210

Required Difference = (1 ÷ 5) × 3210 = 642

**∴ The correct answer is ₹642.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment ratio of X, Y and Z = 32 : 40 : 68

Total profit at the end of the year = ₹3,210

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = Ratio of Investments (when time period is constant)

Share of partner = (Partner's ratio part ÷ Total ratio parts) × Total Profit

 
• 
 
 
 X
 8 parts

 
 Y
 10 parts

 
 Z
 17 parts

 
• 
 
• 
 

 

 Diff = 7 parts

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simplified investment ratio = 32 : 40 : 68 = 8 : 10 : 17

⇒ Let the profits of X, Y and Z be 8k, 10k and 17k respectively.

⇒ Total profit = 8k + 10k + 17k = 35k

⇒ Difference between the shares of Y and Z = 17k − 10k = 7k

⇒ Since 35k = 3210

⇒ 7k = (7 ÷ 35) × 3210

⇒ 7k = (1 ÷ 5) × 3210

⇒ 7k = 642

**∴ The correct answer is ₹642.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When the capital of all partners is invested for the same time period, the total profit or loss is distributed purely in the ratio of their invested capital.

Compound Partnership

When the capital is invested for different time durations, the profit ratio is calculated as the product of capital and time. Profit Ratio = C₁T₁ : C₂T₂ : C₃T₃.

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business operations and receives a fixed salary or a certain percentage of the total profit. A sleeping partner only invests capital. The remaining profit is then distributed among all partners based on their effective investment ratios.
